title: image: support Sigstore bundle verification
body:
Resolves: #388 & https://github.com/ublue-os/main/issues/1477 & https://github.com/coreos/rpm-ostree/issues/5509

Add end-to-end verification of Sigstore bundles attached to container images. The image transport discovers Sigstore artifacts through the registry referrers API, retrieves the bundle, and evaluates its signatures. The implementation supports the bundle formats used by current Sigstore workflows, including DSSE/in-toto payloads, signing certificates, RFC 3161 timestamps, and Rekor evidence.

I tried to split the go dependencies into a seperate commit to make review easier. However, if there is a different prefered method please let me know and I will adjust the PR accordingly.

For the older version of sigstore, we ended up reimplementing parts of the code to avoid that large a dependency chain; that might need to happen here as well — but at this point I have absolutely no opinion on whether / how that should happen.

As someone who worked really hard to reduce dependencies and bloat across our tools I would go as far and say this is a blocker. Even if we ignore the bloat this causes the amount of new repos that will need to be monitored for CVE's and then patched is very hard to justify given the high maintenance this causes.
It is unclear how much of the code in that chain is even actively maintained to me, just from a spot check `go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver` is deprecated.

We’ve had some of these dependencies in the past (e.g. before we replaced the Rekor client), and IIRC a lot of that code is not actually called. But, yes, we did replace the Rekor client, for a reason.

@Luap99 & @mtrmac 100% agree on the dependency bloat. However, I think @mtrmac has identified a potential upstream blocker above that I am going to try to address before continuing to work on bringing the dependency bloat down first.

[sign-container-identity](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/main/cmd/cosign/cli/options/sign.go#L154-L156) appears to have been deprecated: `not possible when OCI referrers become the default behavior`

@mtrmac Should I open an issue upstream with the following question or would you prefer to do it yourself, is there anything else I should add to it?

> With OCI 1.1 referrers, Cosign appears to consider the digest-level referrer relationship sufficient for associating a signature with an image. [podman-container-tools/container-libs](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs), however, deliberately treats the signed manifest digest and signed container identity as separate policy requirements.
> 
> For example, [podman-container-tools/container-libs](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs) uses `pr.SignedIdentity.matchesDockerReference()` to verify that an identity from the signed payload satisfies the configured policy. Depending on the policy, this can require the signed identity to match the repository being pulled (`matchRepository`), match an exact reference (`exactReference`), or match after an explicitly configured identity remapping (`remapIdentity`).
> 
> With the older Cosign simple-signing format, `--sign-container-identity` supplied the signed `docker-reference`, so [podman-container-tools/container-libs](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs) could independently verify both:
> 
> - the signed `docker-manifest-digest` against the manifest being pulled; and
> - the signed `docker-reference` against `pr.SignedIdentity`.
> 
> For example, if the same manifest digest is available as both `quay.io/example/trusted-image@sha256:...` and `registry.example/untrusted-image@sha256:...`, a `matchRepository` policy can distinguish between them based on the identity actually asserted by the signer rather than accepting the signature solely because the content digest matches.
> 
> The new `cosign/sign/v1` statement appears to sign the digest but does not populate `ResourceDescriptor.name` or `uri` with an OCI image identity. The OCI referrer establishes that the signature artifact refers to that digest, but it does not appear to provide the signer-authenticated repository identity needed to perform the `pr.SignedIdentity` check above.
> 
> Is there an intended signed field in `cosign/sign/v1` that consumers such as [podman-container-tools/container-libs](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs) should use for this repository-identity check, or has signer-authenticated container identity intentionally been removed from the new bundle/referrer model?

I really need to catch up on the cosign v3 design before having much of an opinion … at the very least, I think the argument there should be stronger than “container-libs wants it”, something along the lines of https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/2047#issuecomment-1371440193 .
